beats.title: The problem
beats.structureQuote: | 1. The problem | 00:00 | A forager returns; the colony cannot see the resource | `GFX-01` | `CLIP-01`, `CLIP-02`, `CLIP-09`, `CLIP-10` |
beats.opening: A honey bee returns to her colony.
beats.cueQuote: **Beat 1 — the problem.** Opens on `CLIP-01` and `CLIP-02` under the first two paragraphs;

beats.title: Why it is worth an explainer
beats.structureQuote: | 2. Why it is worth an explainer | 01:05 | We can read this signal like an instrument | — | `CLIP-03` |
beats.opening: This is the honey bee waggle dance, and the reason it matters to anyone outside entomology is that it is one of the very few cases in which we can read an animal's signal the way we would read an instrument — where we can say, precisely, what quantity is encoded, in what units, and with what error.

beats.title: The act
beats.structureQuote: | 3. The act | 02:00 | The figure of eight and the waggle run | `GFX-02`, `GFX-03`, `GFX-04` | `CLIP-04`, `CLIP-05`, `CLIP-16` |
beats.opening: A returning forager climbs onto a vertical sheet of comb inside the nest.
beats.cueQuote: **Beat 3 — the act.** `CLIP-04` and `CLIP-16` under the description of the returning forager.

beats.title: Encoding one — direction
beats.structureQuote: | 4. Encoding one — direction | 03:10 | Sun azimuth transposed onto gravity | `GFX-05`, `GFX-06`, `GFX-07`, `GFX-08` | `CLIP-13`, `CLIP-14` |
beats.opening: Take direction first, because it involves a transformation that is easy to state and genuinely strange to think about.
beats.cueQuote: **Beat 4 — direction.** `CLIP-13` and `CLIP-14` establish sun and comb.

beats.title: The moving reference
beats.structureQuote: | 5. The moving reference | 05:10 | Time-compensated solar azimuth, in darkness | `GFX-09` | — |
beats.opening: And there is a complication, which the bee also solves.
beats.cueQuote: **Beat 5 — the moving reference.** `GFX-09` alone, no clip.

beats.title: Encoding two — distance
beats.structureQuote: | 6. Encoding two — distance | 06:15 | Waggle duration; calibrated, not absolute | `GFX-10` | `CLIP-11` |

beats.title: The odometer
beats.structureQuote: | 7. The odometer | 07:20 | Optic flow, and the tunnel experiment | `GFX-11`, `GFX-12`, `GFX-13` | `CLIP-12`, `CLIP-15` |
beats.cueQuote: **Beat 7 — the odometer.** `CLIP-12` and `CLIP-15` under the optic-flow explanation;

beats.title: The vector
beats.structureQuote: | 8. The vector | 08:40 | Two numbers resolving to a region | `GFX-14` | — |
beats.opening: Two numbers, then: an angle against a moving celestial reference, and a duration standing for accumulated optic flow.
beats.cueQuote: **Beat 8 — the vector.** `GFX-14` resolves θ and t into a region with visible extent.

beats.title: Does anything read it
beats.structureQuote: | 9. Does anything read it | 09:05 | Model bee; harmonic radar | `GFX-15`, `GFX-16` | `CLIP-06`, `CLIP-08` |
beats.cueQuote: **Beat 9 — does anything read it.** `CLIP-06` and `CLIP-08` under the attendance description.

beats.title: The error
beats.structureQuote: | 10. The error | 10:40 | Scatter, and the error cone | `GFX-17`, `GFX-18` | `CLIP-07` |

beats.title: Adaptation or constraint
beats.structureQuote: | 11. Adaptation or constraint | 11:30 | The contested question, left contested | `GFX-19` | — |
beats.opening: Whether that imprecision is a limitation or a feature has been argued both ways.

beats.title: What it is worth
beats.structureQuote: | 12. What it is worth | 12:10 | Dance advantage varies by habitat | `GFX-20` | `CLIP-18` |
beats.opening: There is a further result worth knowing, because it puts the whole system in economic terms.
beats.cueQuote: **Beat 12 — what it is worth.** `CLIP-18` under the habitat comparison;

beats.title: The mechanism whole
beats.structureQuote: | 13. The mechanism whole | 12:40 | The block diagram, and the close | `GFX-21`, `GFX-22` | `CLIP-17` |
beats.opening: So, to state the mechanism as a whole.
